== Biography ==
Adam Glasgow was born about 1706 in Stevenston, Ayrshire, Scotland. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1434|John Glasgow]] and [[Cowan-5106|Margaret Cowan]].<ref name="AdamBirth">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZV-BNR : accessed 11 February 2020), John Glasgow in entry for Adam Glasgow, 1706.</ref>

Adam had at least one known brother, John Glasgow, who was born or baptised in Stevenston in 1701.<ref name="JohnBirth">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZK-MY7 : accessed 11 February 2020), John Glasgow, 1701.</ref>

No further details have yet been established with confidence concerning Adam's occupation, marriage, children or death.

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1434]] is assessed at 78% (probable). Adam’s 1706 FamilySearch citation explicitly identifies John Glasgow as father; father-1434 also cites that entry and John 1701, forming a coherent Stevenston adult household. Its identification with the 1679 child remains unproved despite compatible age.

Adult father well supported by attributed entry; complete selected account includes the unproved Kilwinning childhood bridge.

Next useful test: Inspect Adam’s entry and the Cowan marriage/session evidence for a specific childhood-family link.

Source basis already held: [https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZV-BNR "Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564-1950," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYZV-BNR : accessed 11 February 2020), John Glasgow in entry for Adam Glasgow, 1706.]. No new father attached; cited evidence and any inspected register entry are scoped above.



The surviving records of the Stevenston Church of Scotland kirk session include minutes covering 1700–1705.<ref name="StevenstonKirk">National Records of Scotland, "Records for Stevenston," ''Scotland's People'', Stevenston Church of Scotland kirk session, minutes 1700–1705 (https://www.scotlandspeople.gov.uk/place-page/Stevenston/GAZ01016/-/REX01620 : accessed 20 July 2026).</ref>

A secondary account of the kirk-session proceedings states that a John Glasgow of Pipers-Heugh appeared before the session in April 1700. He had requested a testimonial, but it was initially withheld because he was accused of stealing a goose on a Sunday and of being drunk on the preceding Saturday. According to the account, he was publicly rebuked and was then granted the testimonial.<ref name="Piperheugh">"Piperheugh," ''Wikipedia'', section "Micro-history," summarising the Stevenston kirk-session records of April 1700 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Piperheugh : accessed 20 July 2026).</ref>

This John Glasgow was an adult living in Stevenston parish shortly before the recorded births of John Glasgow in 1701 and Adam Glasgow in 1706. He is therefore a possible match for their father, [[Glasgow-1434|John Glasgow]], but no evidence has yet been found connecting the man of Pipers-Heugh directly to Margaret Cowan or her children. The original kirk-session entry should be examined before treating them as the same person.

Pipers-Heugh was a small settlement within Stevenston parish whose inhabitants were historically associated with the manufacture of trumps, also known as Jew's harps.<ref name="Piperheugh" /> There is presently no evidence that Adam or his father worked in that trade.
